//: Lighthouse CI config for the CUSTOMER-FACING web app (theroyalglow.in).
WHY THIS AUDITS web AND NOT admin: Lighthouse measures the public, user-facing
experience — the brand promise in project-overview.md (Lighthouse >= 95
performance, 100 accessibility / SEO). The admin portal is a private,
RBAC-gated internal tool: apps/admin/src/middleware.ts renders NO sign-in and
307-redirects every unauthenticated request to the customer domain (Req 4.7).
An unauthenticated audit of admin.theroyalglow.in therefore measured the
customer homepage under 16 admin URL labels — zero signal about admin — and
failed outright (503) whenever the live deploy or the scale-to-zero Neon
compute was cold. Admin accessibility is instead enforced where it can be
measured honestly: jest-axe assertions on rendered admin components, which run
in the repo-wide unit-tests job.
SELF-CONTAINED, like lighthouserc.docs.json: the web app is built by the CI
step BEFORE LHCI runs (turbo run build --filter=@rgss/web), then
`next start -p 3000` serves that production build and collect.url points at
the local server. So the gate audits THIS PR's code rather than whatever
happens to be deployed, and needs no live environment.
ROUTE LIST: the public, server-rendered pages that render completely without a
session, a database, or a reachable CMS. Every CMS-backed page here
(homepage, /about, /faq, /gallery, /offers) ships a documented fallback when
the CMS is unconfigured or unreachable, so each renders its real content in
CI. Deliberately EXCLUDED: authenticated routes (/profile, /bookings, /gems,
/membership, /favorites, /notifications), /book and /services (their
catalogue/slots come from the DB-backed API, so in CI they would render an
error/empty state rather than the real page), and /blog (Payload-backed
dynamic slugs). Lighthouse CI reports each URL separately, so a sub-threshold
score on ANY audited route fails the matching `categories:*` assertion and
names the offending URL.
THRESHOLDS (project-overview.md 'Premium brand'): performance >= 0.95,
accessibility = 1.0, seo = 1.0, best-practices >= 0.95 — matching the docs
gate rather than the weaker perf >= 0.9 the old admin config used.
